titre: Artefacts · game visual effects made of code
description: A free library of game visual effects written in JavaScript, with no images. Every effect runs live, in the style you pick: pixel, code glyphs, ASCII, braille…
accroche: Game visual effects written in code, shown in the style you pick.
intro: Fire, lightning, explosions, portals, UI… Every effect is a small JavaScript file, with no images, under the MIT license. The style is an option: the same effect shows as pixel art, code glyphs, ASCII, braille or on an old CRT screen.
comparer_texte: Every effect draws into the same pixel buffer. A style is just a filter on top of it: each new style works right away on the whole library, older effects included.
apercu_texte: All 232 effects, organised by tags instead of categories, each with its own number, with bilingual search and favorites.
comment_1: Each effect is a file of a few kilobytes: read it, change it and reuse it in your game.
comment_2: Pixel, glyphs, ASCII, braille, blocks, CRT phosphor… and more to come, with video export and export to Godot.
comment_3: Soon you'll be able to submit your own effects: an editor with live preview, automatic checks and a review before publishing.
pied_licence: Code and effects under the MIT license.
pied_credits: The first 232 effects come from pixelfx (Patch) and the open-source effects of Sprite Fusion (Hugo Duprez).
